title: Restriction of the open Roos comparison through the canonical unit
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each small pro-etale site put $B_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and use the ordinary unbounded module derived category $D(B_W)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Open extension and restriction mean exact ringed-slice functors $e_!\dashv e^*$, applied termwise [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact].
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-open-immersion]. Work with sites small in the fixed module universe; all tower indices are $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. Write $L_W=R\lim$ for total right derived inverse limit on strict towers of $B_W$-modules and use its normalized signed Roos model [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. A strict tower complex $M_\bullet$ has termwise product $P_M=\prod_nM_n$, transition shift $s((x_n)_n)=(d_nx_{n+1})_n$, and signed fiber $\mathsf H(M)^a=P_M^a\oplus P_M^{a-1}$ with differential $(x,y)\mapsto(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$. Here $d_n:M_{n+1}\to M_n$ are the tower transitions. Denote termwise extension by $J$ and termwise restriction by $G$; the same open operations on derived categories are written $j_!$ and $j^*$.
Use the comparisons $\lambda_M:j_!L_UM_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}L_XJM_\bullet$ of [lem-sf-open-roos-extension-comparison]. Let $u:1\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*j_!$ be the actual open adjunction unit, section-normalized to the identity over the open, also termwise on strict systems [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization].
Restriction canonically identifies $j^*B_X=B_U$ and $j^*(A_n)_X=(A_n)_U$, preserving every quotient projection. It is exact and its canonical countable-product comparison is invertible and is the identity on sections over every object $V/U$. There is a specified natural isomorphism
$$\rho_N:j^*L_XN_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}L_UGN_\bullet$$
for every strict tower complex $N_\bullet$ of $B_X$-modules, represented by restriction on both signed Roos summands. For every strict augmentation $c:\Delta D\to N_\bullet$ one has $\rho_N\circ j^*a_c=a_{Gc}$, with the same quotient-unit normalization when $c$ is a quotient augmentation.
For every strict tower complex $M_\bullet$ of $B_U$-modules, the following equality holds in $D(B_U)$:
$$\rho_{JM}\circ j^*(\lambda_M)\circ u_{L_UM}=L_U(u_{M_\bullet}).$$
On the normalized signed Roos models this is the equality with the product of the units $u_{M_n}$ on each of the two summands; the equality preserves all strict augmentations. No tensor factors or constructibility conditions are imposed on the tower complexes.

proof.text: Use the canonical localized-system adjunction to obtain preservation of countable products by its right adjoint. The equation piComparison_comp_π, evaluated on a section over V/U, is exactly the asserted tuple-projection identity. Use sf_clopen_coefficient_comparison for the finite and completed coefficient comparisons, including quotient projections.

An open immersion is a monomorphism. Any two maps V to U over X agree after composition with U to X; cancellation proves that U is subterminal in the pro-etale site. Thus the direct sum defining extension on an object V over U has exactly its structure-arrow summand. The summand injection is an isomorphism. Restriction of that presheaf is the underlying slice sheaf, and cocontinuity of Over.forget commutes its sheafification with restriction. The uniquely normalized actual adjunction unit is this summand injection followed by sheafification, hence invertible. The localization-unit formula gives invertibility of the actual derived unit, first on Q of each complex and then on every object by essential surjectivity. Reuse the proved subterminal module local-calculus unit theorem for this canonical localized adjunction.

Take the shared signed Roos functors, coordinates, normalization isomorphisms, forward comparison, and forward augmentation laws from the open-extension comparison. Its geometry_products supplies exact countable products in both module categories. Apply exactProductFunctorRoosChainMaps to restriction, with these same models in reverse order; this supplies psiG, kappaG, both projection formulas, and naturality. Conjugation by the existing theta isomorphisms followed by full faithfulness of whiskering along Q descends the natural chain comparison to rho. Apply exactProductFunctorRoosCompatibility to get the restriction augmentation law for that rho.

For each signed coordinate and product projection, composing the two diagonal comparison formulas with the actual unit gives GJ(projection) after the unit. Unit naturality identifies this with the projected termwise tower unit. The Roos-map coordinate law identifies the latter with HA of the tower unit. Joint monicity of degreewise product projections and biproduct projections proves the chain-map equality. For every augmentation, the same projection calculation on its coordinates (gamma,0) proves J(b) kappaJ=bJ and G(b) kappaG=bG.

Postcompose the desired derived-unit identity with the isomorphism from the two tower-localization comparisons and thetaA. Naturality of rho moves the first tower comparison, and the two normalized Roos squares cancel the middle thetaB. Unit naturality moves thetaA past the actual derived unit. The explicit localization-unit formula, naturality of mapDerivedCategoryFactors, and the chain-map identity of the preceding step leave thetaA followed by Q(HA(tower unit)). Naturality of thetaA and the localized tower-unit formula identify this with the right-hand side. Cancel the postcomposed isomorphism.
